comment: Context-free translations preserve every visible scalar, finite carrier, PMF, available-set restriction, conditional moment, endpoint condition, and conclusion.

paper_bias.tex_statement:
The fixed-model bias is posterior mean minus true quality:
\[\operatorname{Bias}(\alpha,\beta,\eta,t,q_v)=\frac{\eta\alpha+tq_v}{\eta\alpha+\eta\beta+t}-q_v.\]

paper_facing_eq20_bayesian_rating_equiva.tex_statement: For positive $n$, Equation 20's weighted rating $\frac{n}{n+m}\frac{k}{n}+\frac{m}{n+m}C$ equals $\frac{k+mC}{n+m}$, which is also the binary posterior mean with pseudo-counts $mC$ and $m(1-C)$.

paper_facing_eq21_zero_prior_comparison.tex_statement: Setting every prior pseudo-count to zero in the corrected ordinal posterior rating gives exactly the observed-count average $\frac{\sum_j N_jr_j}{\sum_j N_j}$ printed in Equation 21.

paper_facing_expected_regret.tex_statement: For horizon $T$, nonempty available sets $M_t$, qualities $q$, and selection laws $\pi_t$ supported on $M_t$, regret is $\sum_{t\in\operatorname{Fin}(T)}(\max_{v\in M_t}q(v)-\mathbb E_{v\sim\pi_t}[q(v)])$.

paper_facing_fixed_mse_decomposition.tex_statement: For a finite rating law $\mu$, posterior rating $X$, and true quality $q$, $\mathbb E_\mu[(X-q)^2]=(\mathbb E_\mu[X]-q)^2+\mathbb E_\mu[(X-\mathbb E_\mu[X])^2]$.

paper_facing_individual_producer_unfairn.tex_statement: For the products $S_q=\{v:q_v=q\}$, individual producer unfairness is $\sqrt{|S_q|^{-1}\sum_{v\in S_q}(\operatorname{SR}(v)-\overline{\operatorname{SR}}_q)^2}$, with value zero when $S_q$ is empty.

paper_facing_k_sampling_market_size_is_u.tex_statement: At $k$ equal to the finite market size, the constructed top set is the whole market and the resulting policy is uniform on the whole market.

paper_facing_k_sampling_mechanism.tex_statement: For every sampled score profile and positive $k$ no larger than the finite market size, there exists a nonempty size-$k$ set $T$ whose members weakly dominate every nonmember, and the $k$-sampling policy is uniform on $T$.

paper_facing_k_sampling_one_is_argmax.tex_statement: At $k=1$, the constructed top set is a singleton $\{v\}$, $v$ maximizes the sampled score profile, and the resulting uniform policy is the point mass at $v$.

paper_facing_marketplace_producer_unfair.tex_statement: Marketplace producer unfairness is $\mathbb E_{q\sim\mu_Q}[U(q)]$ for the supplied true-quality law and quality-conditional unfairness function.

paper_facing_selection_rate.tex_statement: A product's selection rate is its number of selections divided by its lifespan, $\operatorname{SR}=s/\ell$.

paper_facing_theorem3_1_squared_bias_non.tex_statement:
If \(\alpha+\beta>0\), \(t>0\), \(0\le \eta_{\mathrm{low}}\), and \(\eta_{\mathrm{low}}\le \eta_{\mathrm{high}}\), then squared bias is nondecreasing in prior strength:
\[\operatorname{Bias}(\alpha,\beta,\eta_{\mathrm{low}},t,q)^2\le
  \operatorname{Bias}(\alpha,\beta,\eta_{\mathrm{high}},t,q)^2.\]

paper_facing_theorem3_1_variance_strict_.tex_statement:
For all parameters, strict variance decrease fails at \(q_v=1\):
\[\neg\bigl(\operatorname{Var}(\alpha,\beta,\eta_{\mathrm{high}},t,1)<
  \operatorname{Var}(\alpha,\beta,\eta_{\mathrm{low}},t,1)\bigr).\]
At this boundary quality the variance term is identically zero.

For all parameters, strict variance decrease fails at \(q_v=0\):
\[\neg\bigl(\operatorname{Var}(\alpha,\beta,\eta_{\mathrm{high}},t,0)<
  \operatorname{Var}(\alpha,\beta,\eta_{\mathrm{low}},t,0)\bigr).\]
At this boundary quality the variance term is identically zero.

If \(\alpha+\beta>0\), \(t>0\), \(0<q<1\), \(0\le \eta_{\mathrm{low}}\), and \(\eta_{\mathrm{low}}<\eta_{\mathrm{high}}\), then variance is strictly decreasing in prior strength:
\[\operatorname{Var}(\alpha,\beta,\eta_{\mathrm{high}},t,q)<
  \operatorname{Var}(\alpha,\beta,\eta_{\mathrm{low}},t,q).\]
The Lean statement makes the interior-quality condition explicit.

paper_facing_theorem3_1_variance_weak_de.tex_statement:
If \(\alpha+\beta>0\), \(t>0\), \(0\le q\le 1\), \(0\le \eta_{\mathrm{low}}\), and \(\eta_{\mathrm{low}}\le \eta_{\mathrm{high}}\), then variance is weakly decreasing in prior strength:
\[\operatorname{Var}(\alpha,\beta,\eta_{\mathrm{high}},t,q)\le
  \operatorname{Var}(\alpha,\beta,\eta_{\mathrm{low}},t,q).\]

paper_facing_theorem3_2_squared_bias_con.tex_statement:
If \(\alpha+\beta>0\), \(\eta\ge 0\), and \(t>0\), then the function
\[q\mapsto \left(\frac{\eta\alpha+tq}{\eta\alpha+\eta\beta+t}-q\right)^2\]
is Jensen-convex. The nonzero denominator follows from these source-domain conditions.

paper_facing_theorem3_2_squared_bias_glo.tex_statement:
If \(\alpha+\beta>0\), \(\eta\ge 0\), and \(t>0\), then the squared-bias function
\[q\mapsto \left(\frac{\eta\alpha+tq}{\eta\alpha+\eta\beta+t}-q\right)^2\]
has a global minimum at \(q=\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)\).

paper_facing_theorem3_2_variance_concave.tex_statement:
If \(t\ge 0\), then the variance function
\[q\mapsto \frac{tq(1-q)}{(\eta\alpha+\eta\beta+t)^2}\]
is Jensen-concave.

paper_facing_theorem3_2_variance_global_.tex_statement:
If \(t\ge 0\), then the variance function
\[q\mapsto \frac{tq(1-q)}{(\eta\alpha+\eta\beta+t)^2}\]
has a global maximum at \(q=1/2\).

paper_facing_thompson_sampling_mechanism.tex_statement:
For a finite nonempty arm set \(V\), belief distribution \(B\) over quality profiles, and policy \(\pi\), Thompson sampling means that there is a tie-breaker \(\tau\) selecting an argmax of each sampled profile and
\[\pi = B.bind\bigl(x\mapsto \operatorname{pure}(\tau(x))\bigr).\]
Equivalently, draw a profile from the belief and select an argmax arm.

paper_fixed_market_mse.tex_statement: For a finite nonempty product set $V$, fixed-market MSE is $|V|^{-1}\sum_{v\in V}(\widehat q(v)-q(v))^2$.

paper_ordinal_posterior_rating.tex_statement: For finite ordinal categories $j$, rating values $r_j$, prior pseudo-counts $\widehat\alpha_j$, and observed counts $N_j$, the corrected posterior expected rating is $\frac{\sum_j(\widehat\alpha_j+N_j)r_j}{\sum_j(\widehat\alpha_j+N_j)}$.

paper_posterior_mean.tex_statement:
For prior-shape variables \((\alpha,\beta)\), prior strength \(\eta\), review count \(t\), and true quality \(q_v\), the Lean definition is
\[\widehat q_v(\alpha,\beta,\eta,t,q_v)=\frac{\eta\alpha+tq_v}{\eta\alpha+\eta\beta+t}.\]
The docstring identifies \((\alpha,\beta)\) with the paper's \((\widetilde\alpha,\widetilde\beta)\).

paper_posterior_rating.tex_statement: For prior parameters $\widehat\alpha,\widehat\beta$ and natural counts $R\le |S|$, the posterior rating is $(\widehat\alpha+R)/(\widehat\alpha+\widehat\beta+|S|)$.
